baddieapple is an exploit that allows for code execution in miniOS while the developer switch is set to on (after the original baddieapple patch).
A ChromeOS device running a version between 133 and 142 A USB drive (8GB or larger) A separate computer to prepare the USB drive
Download a baddieapple image for your board from dl.crosbreaker.com. Once you have this image, follow the flashing guide to flash it to your USB drive.
Once the image is flashed, press Esc + Refresh + Power on your keyboard. When the recovery page appears, insert your USB drive.

Once recovery finishes, press Esc + Refresh + Power again. Then press Ctrl + D, followed by Enter. When you reach the "developer mode is blocked" screen, press Esc + Refresh + Power, then select "recovery using an internet connection." Once the menu loads fully, press Ctrl + Alt + F3 (commonly the fullscreen key). You will now have a shell that can be used to perform other exploits. If you were directed here by another exploit document, return to that document to continue.
badsh1mmer is a modified recovery image exploit that leverages the ChromeOS recovery process to unenroll managed devices. It works by modifying a recovery image to gain a root shell.
A ChromeOS device that has completed sh1ttyOOBE or sh1ttyexec A USB drive (8GB or larger) A separate computer to prepare the USB drive A compatible modified recovery image for your board
This exploit works on all boards (*) within the supported version range. If your device's platform version falls within the range shown above, it should be compatible.
Download the appropriate recovery image for your board from the crosbreaker file host.
Turn off your Chromebook Hold Esc + Refresh and press Power to enter recovery mode Press Ctrl + D and then Enter Insert the prepared USB drive Press Esc + Refresh and press Power again to boot
Once booted, you should see a menu. Using the options available, you can unenroll your device.

Issue Solution Device doesn't boot from USB Ensure the USB was flashed correctly and try a different USB port "ChromeOS is missing or damaged" This is expected — insert your prepared USB drive "Device owner requires this device to run with ChromeOS verification on" sh1ttyexec was unsuccessful — redo sh1ttyexec
Pseudounenrollment until next powerwash on verified boot R126-R127. Requires an Android phone.
A ChromeOS device running a version on 126 or 127 An Android phone

Powerwash your Chromebook Connect to Wi-Fi from quick settings (Shift + Alt + S) Press Ctrl + Alt + Q and click "Get started" Select "Transfer Wi-Fi from phone" Connect your phone from the popup Scan the QR code and complete the fingerprint verification Select "Transfer Wi-Fi from phone" again Close the app on your phone Log in to your Google account Complete the Chromebook setup Press Ctrl + Shift + Q + Q Press "Get started" Press "Next" — you should see three sign-in options. Choose the first one, then log in to gain persistence
Sign out You should be back on the setup screen Continue and add your personal account It will now persist until the next powerwash

After completing the persistent method, you can recover to modified recovery images in unverified recovery because VPD is not blocking developer mode. This can be used to obtain a root shell even on keyrolled devices via badshimmer, but cannot remove FWMP on KV5. Currently, this is used to remove FWMP on keyrolled Dedede Chromebooks on KV4 with an Android phone. See dededeicarus for more information.

sh1mmer is a shim-based exploit that uses a modified debugging tool intended for repair centers. It allows for code execution and includes many unenrollment exploit payloads built in.
A USB drive or SD card (8GB or larger recommended) A separate computer to prepare the USB drive (Linux, Windows, macOS, or another ChromeOS device)

This exploit works on all boards with a RMA shim that don't have the key-roll patch. Keyrolling affects most nissas & corsolas, and some dededes. If your device's board is within the list shown below, it should be compatible. ambassador, banon, brask, brya, clapper, coral, corsola, cyan, dedede, edgar, elm, enguarde, fizz, glimmer, grunt, hana, hatch, jacuzzi, kalista, kefka, kukui, lulu, nami, nissa, octopus, orco, puff, pyro, reef, reks, relm, sand, sentry, snappy, stout, strongbad, tidus, trogdor, ultima, volteer, zork
Download the appropriate SH1MMER prebuilt image for your board from the crosbreaker downloads page. Make sure to download the correct image for your specific board codename.

Turn off your Chromebook completely Plug in your flash drive containing the SH1MMER image Press [Esc + Refresh + Power] to enter recovery mode When you see the recovery screen, press [Ctrl + D] to enable developer mode Press [Esc + Refresh + Power] again and allow the shim to boot up The SH1MMER menu should appear on your screen.
Open the payloads menu Select the payload that your device is affected by (most likely quicksilver) Execute it Assuming it doesn't exit and reboot for you, continue to step 5
Select "Exit" from the SH1MMER menu Your Chromebook will reboot Your device should now be unenrolled
sh1ttyexec is an exploit that allows code execution on keyrolled Chromebooks with kernel version 6 by crashing the OOBE and booting an unverified recovery image. This was patched in v143.
A ChromeOS device running a version between 133 and 142 A USB drive (8GB or larger)

Powerwash the device Begin enrolling the device, then open the powerwash menu with Ctrl + Alt + Shift + R on the enrollment screen (not the "Please wait" screen). Wait until it crashes back to OOBE Try enrolling again, but the moment the enrollment screen appears (the screen that says "Enrollment," not "Please wait"), press Esc + Refresh + Power This step is timing-sensitive, so don't expect to get it on the first try. Once successful, block_devmode is set to 0.
Press Esc + Refresh + Power to enter recovery mode Press Ctrl + D and then Enter Press Esc + Refresh + Power again and plug in your USB drive From here, you can proceed with badshimmer.

Turn off your Chromebook completely Plug in your flash drive containing the SH1MMER image Press [Esc + Refresh () + Power ()] to enter recovery mode When you see the recovery screen, press [Ctrl + D] to enable developer mode Press [Esc + Refresh + Power] again and allow the shim to boot up Cr3nroll's menu should appear on your screen, use the arrow keys and enter key to navigate it.
From Cr3nroll's menu, select "Deprovision/Unenroll" Follow any on-screen prompts Wait for the process to complete

Developer mode allows you to execute code natively in chromeOS, disable write protect (allowing for unkeyrolling [TODO, WRITE UNKEYROLLING DOC AND LINK IT HERE] and flashing GBB flags), and modify chromeOS to your heart's content.

Boot into Recovery by pressing [Esc + Refresh + Power] Press [Ctrl+D], then enter On the devmode bootsplash, you can press several key combinations to do different things. [Ctrl+D] to boot from internal disk (chromeOS) [Ctrl+U] to boot from external disk (recovery image, shim, chromiumOS, etc..) [Ctrl+L] to boot with alternate firmware (linux off a usb, or if you've installed linux to the internal disk it will boot that)
Open a virtual terminal (numbered 1-4) by pressing [Ctrl + Alt + F#] (where # is the number). Log in as root or chronos. Run commands.

Platform version: 0.0.0 – 9999.9999.9999 Boards: * This guide covers how to flash ChromeOS recovery shims and images to USB drives or SD cards. Most crosbreaker exploits require flashing a modified recovery shim or recovery image to a USB drive before booting it on your Chromebook.

USB drive or SD card: 8GB or larger recommended The image file: Downloaded from dl.crosbreaker.com A computer: Can be Windows, macOS, Linux, or ChromeOS Important Flashing will erase all data on your USB drive. Back up any important files before proceeding.

(The easiest method if you're using a ChromeOS device.) Install the Chromebook Recovery Utility from the Chrome Web Store Open the extension and click the gear icon in the top-right corner Select "Use local image" Click "Select" and choose your downloaded .bin file Insert your USB drive when prompted Select your USB drive from the list Click "Continue" and wait for the flashing process to complete You'll see a success message when done. Remove the USB drive. Alternatively, if booting developer mode: Open VT2 [Ctrl+Alt+F2] Login as root. See dd instructions under Linux.

Download balenaEtcher from etcher.balena.io Install and run balenaEtcher Insert your USB drive In Etcher: Click "Flash from file" and select your .bin file Click "Select target" and choose your USB drive Click "Flash!" Wait for flashing and verification to complete Safely eject your USB drive

Download balenaEtcher from etcher.balena.io Open the downloaded .dmg and drag Etcher to Applications Launch balenaEtcher Insert your USB drive In Etcher: Click "Flash from file" and select your .bin file Click "Select target" and choose your USB drive Click "Flash!" Enter your password when prompted (required for disk access) Wait for the process to complete Eject your USB drive

Download balenaEtcher from etcher.balena.io Make it executable: chmod +x balenaEtcher-*.AppImage Run Etcher: ./balenaEtcher-*.AppImage Insert your USB drive In Etcher: Click "Flash from file" and select your .bin file Click "Select target" and choose your USB drive Click "Flash!" Wait for the process to complete Eject your USB drive

Insert your USB drive Find your USB drive: lsblk or sudo fdisk -l Look for your USB drive (usually /dev/sdb or /dev/sdc) Unmount the drive (if auto-mounted): sudo umount /dev/sdX* Replace X with your drive letter Flash the image: sudo dd if=/path/to/image.bin of=/dev/sdX bs=4M status=progress oflag=sync Replace /path/to/image.bin with your actual file path Replace /dev/sdX with your USB drive (e.g., /dev/sdb) bs=4M sets block size for faster writing status=progress shows progress oflag=sync ensures data is written before completion Wait for completion (typically 3-10 minutes depending on USB speed) Sync and eject: sync sudo eject /dev/sdX Critical Warning Using the wrong device (e.g., /dev/sda instead of /dev/sdb) will overwrite your system drive and destroy your OS. Always double-check with lsblk before running dd. note Different exploits may have additional requirements or steps.

Platform version: 0.0.0 – 99999.9999.9999 Boards: * This guide will cover: What GBB and FWMP are How to set/wipe GBB flags How to safely (temporarily) re-enroll How to undo all your changes for if you need to eventually turn in your device

FWMP are Firmware Management Parameters, and their most important behavior is that they block devmode on the firmware level (not OS level). On the OS level, devmode is blocked by a key in RW_VPD called block_devmode. When it's set to 1, booting devmode will error (see below). If it's blocked by FWMP instead, you'll instead never get the option to boot ChromeOS in devmode and be greeted with this: So in order to boot devmode, you need two things: FWMP cleared (more specifically, must not have the flag 0x01) block_devmode=0 in RW_VPD.

(For a more comprehensive understanding, see OlyB's GBB-flag-inator) All you need to know is that the GBB flags 0xa0b1 override the FWMP flag 0x1, meaning devmode is not firmware-blocked even if enrolled. (It also makes devmode auto-boot in 2 seconds instead of 30, and removes the beep when auto-booting. You can stop auto booting by pressing another key). Putting this together, it means so long as GBB flags are set and you use some form of code execution to set block_devmode=0, you can unenroll extremely easily on any version! The issue? In order to set GBB flags, write protect must be disabled (meaning you must already be unenrolled), so this isn't an unenrollment exploit (at least, not the first time around, still makes future unenrollments easier).
Disabling WP is outside the scope of this guide, but instructions on how to do so can be found on MrChromebox's site.

Once WP is disabled, open VT2 as root (see the Developer Mode guide if you don't know how) To set GBB flags, run: futility gbb -s --flash --flags=0xa0b1 # use whatever flags you prefer if you know what you're doing To wipe GBB flags and re-enable WP futility gbb -s --flash --flags=0x0000 flashrom --wp-enable If you're wiping your traces, I also suggest picking up the latest recovery image from https://cros.download/recovery and flashing it, and of course going through OOBE in verified mode so you get re-enrolled.

As previously outlined, it is significantly easier to unenroll again if you've set GBB flags. So before re-enrolling, check two things: Ensure you have actually set GBB flags set by booting recovery and pressing [Tab], you should see a line that says gbb.flags: 0x0000a0b1 (or anything with at least 0xa090). Ensure you are NOT in developer mode before re-enrolling, this will set off an alarm in your sysadmin's Google Admin Console. To check, try pressing [Ctrl+Alt+F2] before pressing "Get Started" in OOBE. If it does take you to the developer console, you're in devmode and need to go back to verified mode. (You can do this by rebooting, and either following the steps to turn on "OS verification" or "Return to secure mode"). After that's said and done, go through OOBE as normal and you should be force re-enrolled. From there, you're ready to take your kiosk exam or whatever else you need to be enrolled for.

After safely re-enrolling, you'll want to uneneroll again (that's the entire point of setting GBB flags after all). To do so, do the following: Plug in usb with a shim You can boot shims even if keyrolled with usb boot Boot developer mode (firmware level, not chromeOS) Hit [Ctrl+U] (it will USB boot) Open the shell and run the following commands: vpd -i RW_VPD -s block_devmode=0 crossystem block_devmode=0 Reboot, unplug the usb, and let developer mode (chromeOS) boot. You should not get the OS level block message, and will instead boot normal devmode chromeOS. Make sure to prevent re-enrollment!
After unenrolling, you may want to prevent your device from accidentally re-enrolling.
Open VT2 [Ctrl+Alt+F2], log in as root, then run the following: mount --bind /dev/null /tmp/machine-info initctl restart ui
Return to the UI [Ctrl+Alt+F1]. Ignore any popups about broken device identifiers, then OOBE will complete without any enrollment checks. If it still enrolls, please ask in our discord for help.
Skiovox is an exploit that abuses kiosk apps having different policies that are usually far more unrestricted compared to normal user accounts.
A ChromeOS device running a version on 141 or below A website kiosk app
This exploit supports any device as long as you are on ChromeOS 141 or below.

Sign out of your Chromebook with Ctrl + Shift + Q + Q Look in the bottom left corner of the screen and find the Apps button Click on Apps Find one of the following kiosk apps: Riverside Datamanager Bluebook College Board TestNav Open the kiosk app and ensure it is a website kiosk app. To verify, check if there is a link below the name of the kiosk app while it is loading Find a way to navigate to Google or GitHub from within the kiosk app tip If you need help navigating to a search engine, join the crosbreaker Discord server and check the pins in the "Skiovox on <142" thread.

protowrite is an exploit for ChromeOS devices that can create & write to any r/w file. By writing an unusable re_enrollment_key to /run/vpd/ro.txt, it unpatches Quicksilver and unenrolls on devices v135 to v145.

A ChromeOS device running a ChromeOS version between 135 and 145 Some form of code execution (if you're lucky enough to be on unkeyrolled nissa, you can use sh1mmer instead of baddieapple). Note You also need to be somewhat lucky to have access to baddieapple, see (codenerd add your doc's link here)
caution This exploit is ONLY doable on nissa, skywalker, and rauru!!

Enter baddieapple, but connect to the internet before entering VT3 Critical Warning DO NOT let it begin recovering, hit back after connecting to the internet. If it begins to recover, hit [Esc+Refresh+Power] immediately. Open VT3 to gain access to a shell. Run the following command: curl -Lsk ba.crosbreaker.com/protowrite.sh | sh After it performs the "critical update" (stateful key migration), enter baddieapple again. Quicksilver is an exploit that was introduced due to Google failing to properly implement re-enrollment keys for ChromeOS Flex (the UEFI variant of ChromeOS, able to be installed on any PC). Specifically, they made re_enrollment_key both exist in normal ChromeOS AND take precedence over normal values that force re-enrollment such as stable device secret and serial number.
A ChromeOS device running a ChromeOS version between 125 and 142 A USB drive (8GB or larger) A separate computer to prepare the USB drive
This exploit supports any board that has the OS versions 125-142.
Download baddieapple for your board from our download site.

See the flashing guide tip Since you're using baddieapple, it will recover like normal. This is intended. See the badapple repo (TODO, WRITE BADAPPLE DOC) for steps on how to get to the shell after recovering.
run the following commands vpd -i RW_VPD -s re_enrollment_key=$(openssl rand -hex 32) crossystem disable_dev_request=1 reboot -f
After rebooting you should be in OOBE in secure mode (if not, return to secure mode). Proceed through OOBE and FWMP will be removed, thus allowing you to boot devmode.

Select payloads Select quicksilver Follow the prompts' instructions tip If it says you're on 143+ but you know you aren't, override it, badsh1mmer sh is weird and tends to be somewhat buggy, though it should all be fixed at this point. After rebooting you should be in OOBE in secure mode (if not, return to secure mode). Proceed through OOBE and FWMP will be removed, thus allowing you to boot devmode.
Open a shell and run the following command: vpd -i RW_VPD -d re_enrollment_key Alternatively, update to 143+ instead.

Cr3nroll-shim is a shim-based utility, therefore it does not work on keyrolled devices. It allows for easy management of enrollment and unenrollment on supported versions. Unenrollment is done within Cr3nroll-shim via Quicksilver!

This utility works on all boards with a RMA shim that don't have the key-roll patch. Keyrolling affects most nissas & corsolas, and some dededes. If your device's board is within the list shown below, it should be compatible. ambassador, banon, brask, brya, clapper, coral, corsola, cyan, dedede, edgar, elm, enguarde, fizz, glimmer, grunt, hana, hatch, jacuzzi, kalista, kefka, kukui, lulu, nami, nissa, octopus, orco, puff, pyro, reef, reks, relm, sand, sentry, snappy, stout, strongbad, tidus, trogdor, ultima, volteer, zork
Download the appropriate Cr3nroll prebuilt image for your board from the Cr3nroll-shim github. Make sure to download the correct image for your specific board codename.

Turn off your Chromebook completely Plug in your flash drive containing the SH1MMER image Press [Esc + Refresh () + Power ()] to enter recovery mode When you see the recovery screen, press [Ctrl + D] to enable developer mode Press [Esc + Refresh + Power] again and allow the shim to boot up Cr3nroll's menu should appear on your screen, use the arrow keys and enter key to navigate it.

From Cr3nroll's menu, select "Deprovision/Unenroll" Follow any on-screen prompts Wait for the process to complete Exit Cr3nroll (press exit) Return to secure mode and press "Get started" in the oobe. then you're done!

The Ti50's AP Read-Only Verification (APROV) does not check the RO_VPD region, allowing any user to unenroll the device by changing the stable device secret with a flash programmer. Cr50 has no APROV, so this works on it too.

An external flash programmer (and a 1.8V adapter if your flash chip is 1.8V instead of 3.3V) and the appropriate hardware to interface to the SPI flash chip. A ch347 or ch341a are most common, however, others such as ft232h and raspberry pi's can also be used ch347 is STRONGLY preferred over ch341a since it is much faster and has the correct I/O voltage without modding it (update: this was incorrect. ch341a switches the data lines to 3.3V when actually in use) A Linux machine and root access to program the target device A willingness/ability to open up the target device EXPERIENCE WITH LINUX AND A BRAIN. WE WILL NOT TEACH YOU LINUX. DO NOT ASK FOR SUPPORT.

This will work on any board that utilizes the Dauntless Google Security Chip (running Ti50 Firmware). This can also be used to set GBB flags on any board running Cr50 Firmware due to the lack of APROV. Critical Warning If you are at all inexperienced or otherwise don't know what you're doing, DO NOT PROCEED. You will likely brick your device. This isn't as risky as pencil method, but it's still better to be safe than sorry.

note For both types of SPI flash chips, they tend to have WINBOND or GIGADEVICE branding, and typically say 25Q64[xx] or 25Q128[xx] (or 25Q256) under the branding. DO NOT touch the EC chip, which has W25X40[xx]. Pin 1 corresponds with a circle or indent on the chip itself, attach the clip/probe accordingly. If your chromebook has a SOIC-8 flash chip, then a ch347/ch341a (with a SOIC-8 clip) will work. Seeing as ch347 is 20 times faster, we will assume you are using it. AliExpress: note A general AliExpress rule is to only buy it if it has a review from the last couple months, (where more recent is better), also a higher number of purchases is often better. ch347: search for "ch347 programmer" Often you will get results for xtw-3, xtw-5, xtw100, and ch347 as different "colors", pick ch347 1.8v adapter: search for "1.8v adapter" Make sure you get the one with an ALVC164245 chip WSON-8 probe: search for "wson probe", make sure you get one with pogo pins and plastic baffle Make sure you get the right size!! 6x5mm = 6.5mm spacing, 8x6mm = 8.5mm spacing DigiKey/Mouser: SOIC-8 clip: https://www.digikey.com/en/products/detail/pomona-electronics/5250/745102 or https://www.mouser.com/ProductDetail/Pomona-Electronics/5250?qs=q2OAyjihNMzqkARxZuX5AQ%3D%3D Before Proceeding Look up the part number of your flash chip to determine which voltage it needs. The ch347 switches from the USB's 5V to 3.3V, however, many chromebook flash chips use 1.8V. USE THE 1.8V ADAPTER IF NEEDED.

Install flashrom if you don't have it already for some reason. In order to modify the VPD on your linux machine, you will need to compile vpd from source. The reason we use such an old version is that google removed the Makefile way back in version 118, so you have to build from 117 git clone https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromiumos/platform/vpd \ --branch release-R117-15572.B cd vpd make sudo chmod +x vpd # optional, you can just type the path to the vpd binary if you want sudo cp vpd /usr/local/bin/

note These commands are assuming you are using a ch347 programmer, adjust accordingly. Power off the chromebook, then remove the chassis. IMPORTANT: Unplug the battery before doing anything with the internal hardware Attach the chip clip or probe to the flash chip. caution Many devices have the flash chip on the top side of the motherboard, requiring removing it from the chromebook completely. This doesn't make doing this impossible, but you will have to re-assemble afterwards. Be advised this is not a comprehensive guide on how to attach a flash programmer. See the user manual with the kit you bought, or look it up. Remove software write protection using flashrom: flashrom -p ch347_spi --wp-disable Read the firmware and back it up: flashrom -p ch347_spi -r coreboot.bin cp coreboot.bin coreboot.bin.bak # KEEP THIS BACKUP IF YOU WANT TO RE-ENROLL # optionally, also back up the sds to a text file vpd -f coreboot.bin.bak \ -g stable_device_secret_DO_NOT_SHARE > vpd.txt Change the stable device secret: vpd -f coreboot.bin \ -s stable_device_secret_DO_NOT_SHARE=$(openssl rand -hex 32) Write the modified firmware back to the device: flashrom -p ch347_spi -w coreboot.bin caution If you skip this next step (and your chromebook uses Ti50), your device will be unbootable, so do it. Re-enable software WP. flashrom -p ch347_spi --wp-enable Go through the normal enrollment process and you will be unenrolled.
